title: Finite Hom estimate for universal small etale integral reductions
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, I=(v) generated by a nonzerodivisor, and R/I finite. Let X be a finite-type scheme over a field k [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with the exponent of R/I invertible on k. Work in the small etale derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix n>=0. Let K,L be arbitrary R-complexes whose underlying R-derived reductions modulo I^(n+1) are bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and have R-Tor amplitudes [a,b] and [c,e] [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. If dim X <= d [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then the underlying R-reduction modulo I^(n+1) of RHom_R(K,L) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is bounded constructible and has R-Tor amplitude in [c-b-2d,e-a+2d]. This is a single finite-level statement; it assumes no derived completeness, no uniform intervals over all levels, and no Noetherian or domain condition on R.

source.place: sentences 2-4, finite-level constructibility and uniform Hom interval; constant-coefficient small etale specialization; regular coefficient resolution from lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction.proof.md

proof.text: The quotient A=R/I^(n+1) is finite: filter by powers of v and use the finite R/I subquotients. For each residue field F of A, the regular two-term resolution shows A tensor_R F is F[1] direct-sum F. By derived tensor associativity, the underlying R-reduction bound [a,b], tested on the constant F-sheaf, forces K tensor_R F to have cohomology in [a+1,b]. The universal scalar reduction identifies this with Kn tensor_A F; similarly Ln has residue bounds [c+1,e]. Use the finite-length filtration by the radical of each local Artinian factor to promote the residue bounds to the quotient Tor intervals [a+1,b] and [c+1,e]. Constructibility of Kn,Ln is checked on their exact scalar restrictions. This is the finite ring residue-test argument, not an assumption of DVR structure or completeness. Unit ideal and reversed intervals give zero.

On affine opens after an algebraic closure of k, use the finite-Tor constructible Hom estimate for a finite coefficient ring, by its dual-tensor-dual proof. With step 1 its quotient Tor interval is [c+1-b-2d,e-a-1+2d]. Descend from the field extension and glue over the affine opens. Restriction to R uses the regular two-term coefficient resolution and gives [c-b-2d,e-a-1+2d], contained in the asserted interval. Restriction is exact and preserves constructible homology. Universality identifies arbitrary Kn,Ln with the quotient models. Finally the scalar adjunction and the regular coefficient triangle identify this restricted finite Hom with the ambient Hom reduction. This single-level estimate has no completeness or uniform tower clause.

theorem integralFiniteHomEstimate
    {R : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    [Finite (R ⧸ I)]
    {v : R} (hv : v ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) (hI : I = Ideal.span {v})
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [HasInvertibleExponent (R ⧸ I) (Spec (.of k))]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (aX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType aX] [QuasiCompact aX] (n : ℕ)
    {K L : D(X, R)}
    (hK : DerivedCategory.boundedConstructible (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X
      ((reductionModIdeal R X (I ^ (n + 1))).obj K))
    (hL : DerivedCategory.boundedConstructible (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X
      ((reductionModIdeal R X (I ^ (n + 1))).obj L))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (a b c e : ℤ)
    (hKt : DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X a b
      ((reductionModIdeal R X (I ^ (n + 1))).obj K))
    (hLt : DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X c e
      ((reductionModIdeal R X (I ^ (n + 1))).obj L))
    : DerivedCategory.boundedConstructible (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X
        ((reductionModIdeal R X (I ^ (n + 1))).obj
          (((derivedHom (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X).obj (op K)).obj L)) ∧
      DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X
        (c - b - 2 * (d : ℤ)) (e - a + 2 * (d : ℤ))
        ((reductionModIdeal R X (I ^ (n + 1))).obj
          (((derivedHom (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) X).obj (op K)).obj L))
